html:
The Ngäbe and the Buglé are two Indigenous peoples of western Panama who speak related Chibchan languages. The Ngäbe, once called Guaymí, are the largest Indigenous people of Panama, and their communities also reach into Costa Rica.

They live in the mountains and along the Caribbean coast, farming maize, rice, beans and plantains. Since the 1900s many have worked on banana and coffee plantations, and each harvest season thousands cross into Costa Rica to pick coffee. In 1997 Panama created the Ngäbe-Buglé comarca, a self-governing territory. In 2012 Ngäbe protesters blocked the Pan-American Highway against mining and dam projects on their land. Their Chibchan relatives include the Bribri; to the east live the Wounaan.
